user_prompt: Demo the new signup flow on our staging site. Show it off like a recruiter would watch it.

slides.frame: Logged-out homepage. Hero with a single 'Sign up free' CTA above the fold.
slides.moment: The hero is doing one job: get you to sign up. No carousel, no marketing tour.

slides.frame: Signup modal opens inline (no page reload). Three fields: email, password, workspace name. Password strength meter live.
slides.moment: Three fields total. Password meter is live, not on submit.

slides.frame: Submitted with a weak password. Inline red helper text appears under the password field; submit button stays disabled until strength is acceptable.
slides.moment: Error is right where the field is, no scroll, no toast.

slides.frame: Verification email screen. Big preview of the email that was sent, with a 'Resend' control and a 'change email' link.
slides.moment: Shows you the actual email preview so you know what to look for in inbox.

user_prompt: QA the checkout flow on staging. Smoke test the happy path plus the obvious failure modes.
audience: another engineer reviewing the QA pass

slides.frame: Cart page. Two items, subtotal $48, free-shipping banner triggered at $50 threshold.
slides.moment: Cart loaded clean. Free-shipping prompt appears at the right threshold.

slides.frame: Checkout page. Address autocomplete worked on a known address. Payment defaults to saved card.
slides.moment: Address autocomplete and saved-card default both worked first try.

slides.frame: Submitted with an expired card on purpose. Got a clear inline error 'Card expired — try another' and no charge attempted (verified via /admin).
slides.moment: Expired-card failure mode handled cleanly. No charge attempted.

slides.frame: Re-submitted with valid card. Order-confirmation page renders, order ID is real, confirmation email triggers in test inbox.
slides.moment: Happy path passed end-to-end. Order ID and email both real.

slides.frame: Refresh after success. Cart is cleared. Back button does not re-submit the order.
slides.moment: Post-success state is clean. No accidental re-submit on back.

user_prompt: Make a guide showing how to inspect a real internet traffic shift using Cloudflare Radar.
audience: AI engineer or product-minded builder who has not used Radar before

slides.frame: Cloudflare Radar open to the worldwide HTTP traffic chart, default 7-day view.
slides.moment: Start on a chart that already shows a signal. The dashboard tour adds nothing.

slides.frame: Switched the comparison geography from worldwide to Germany. Chart now overlays the two and a clear divergence appears in the last 48 hours.
slides.moment: One filter change reveals a real divergence between worldwide and Germany.

slides.frame: Changed time window from 7 days to 90 days. Divergence persists, so this is not a one-off spike.
slides.moment: Time-window check confirms this is a sustained shift, not a blip.

slides.frame: Drilled into the AS-level breakdown for Germany. One specific ISP shows the bulk of the change.
slides.moment: AS-level breakdown localizes the change to a single ISP.

slides.frame: Held on the AS-level chart with the ISP highlighted. The pattern is obvious and the chart stands alone.
slides.moment: The final chart explains itself. This is the frame to send.

user_prompt: Repro the 503 on signup that QA flagged this morning.
audience: the engineer who has to fix this

slides.frame: Cleared cookies and local storage. Cold-loaded /signup on staging.
slides.moment: Fresh session. No leftover auth state.

slides.frame: Submitted the form with valid data. Network panel shows POST /api/auth/signup returning 503.
slides.moment: 503 reproduces on first try with valid input.

slides.frame: Inspected the response body. Stack trace mentions a missing Redis rate-limit key 'auth:signup:global'.
slides.moment: Root cause appears to be a missing rate-limit Redis key.
